issues.legal_issue: A temporary injunction may be maintained where the claimant presents a prima facie claim supported by a legally effective sale certificate and official records indicating possession, without finally resolving disputed title at the interlocutory stage.
material_facts: The claimant sought a declaration of ownership and possession, and an injunction against interference, in a suit concerning disputed land.
The claimant relied on a sale certificate issued after an auction in a recovery proceeding; the certificate was later amended to include the disputed land.
Official records of rights indicated that the claimant was in possession.
The sale certificate had not been set aside or declared a nullity, and the competing claims raised serious issues for determination in the suit.
issues.conclusion: The appellate court correctly maintained the temporary injunction, and the appeals challenging that order were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: A court should not conduct a mini trial when deciding whether to grant a temporary injunction. A sale certificate retains legal validity and force unless set aside or declared a nullity, and rights may be derived from it. Possession indicated by records of rights cannot, at this stage, simply be treated as that of a trespasser where the claimant asserts possession in their own right. The judgment identifies no earlier case as authority for these propositions. The reference to Section 31 of the State Financial Corporations Act, 1951, concerns the recovery proceeding in which the auction took place, rather than the injunction principle applied.

rule.if: interlocutory_injunction_appeal and prima_facie_sale_certificate_supports_claim and possession_records_support_claim and sale_certificate_not_invalidated

predicates.interlocutory_injunction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging an order on an application for temporary injunction in a pending suit.
predicates.prima_facie_sale_certificate_supports_cl: The claimant relies on a sale certificate issued after an auction that, on its face, supports a claim to the disputed property.
predicates.possession_records_support_claim: Official records indicate that the claimant is in possession of the disputed property.
predicates.sale_certificate_not_invalidated: The sale certificate has not been set aside or declared a nullity.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a temporary injunction and the claimant's property claim is supported by a sale certificate and possession records, and the certificate remains uninvalidated, the injunction is maintained without finally deciding title.
